subject: RFP: Data stewardship, snapshot access & preservation schedule
messages:
From: Martin Green <mgreen@triadbank.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lopez <s.lopez@triadbank.com>, rdp-legal@triadbank.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: Data stewardship, snapshot access & preservation schedule

Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our RFP. To evaluate Redwood for our custody and compliance needs we need more granular responses on the following items (we will fold these into the formal questionnaire):

1) Retention windows: list retention default and configurable ranges for audit logs, request/response bodies, KV caches, and ephemeral prompt history. Please identify which classes are retained by default and which require customer configuration or Dedicated/Private deployment.

2) Snapshot & exportability: describe mechanical steps to produce point-in-time snapshots for a given tenant (time to produce, formats, schema, chain-of-custody evidence). Can we request incremental versus full snapshots?

3) Redaction & DSARs: how do you support on-demand redaction for PII/PCI/PHI, and what export formats preserve redaction provenance?

4) Tamper evidence & integrity: what cryptographic or timestamping controls are available to demonstrate immutability of exported records? Any support for verifiable hashes or ledgering?

5) SLAs & delivery timelines: if Triad Bank requests a forensic handoff, what are standard delivery SLAs (standard vs expedited) and what delivery methods (S3 transfer, encrypted bundle via secure FTP, customer-managed key export)?

6) Roles & access: who can trigger exports? can we audit the operator who created an export? Provide a sample ACL and audit sample.

7) Cost & operational constraints: typical cost drivers (GB exported, compute to assemble snapshots), any throttle windows, and if exports impact live serving latency.

We'd appreciate a short matrix for each item and any example or stub runbooks you can share. Targeting an internal decision by the week of 2026-09-06, so an initial reply within two business days would be ideal.

Best,
Martin Green
Head of Cloud Compliance — Triad Bank

[Attachment: Triad_RFP_Appendix_A.pdf (pdf)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Green <mgreen@triadbank.com>
Cc: Sarah Lopez <s.lopez@triadbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Data stewardship, snapshot access & preservation schedule

Martin —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a compact Retention_Spec_Matrix.xlsx and a short summary. We can produce a fuller runbook if you want an auditable artifact.

1) Retention windows
- Audit logs (control plane): default 13 months for Hosted; Dedicated/Private configurable 30/90/365/indefinite. Retention is tenant-configurable via Console or API (requires owner role).
- Request/response bodies (payloads): default 30 days for Hosted anonymized; Dedicated & Private can be set to 0 / 30 / 90 / 365 / indefinite. Note: request/response bodies are considered higher-sensitivity and have separate encryption-at-rest keys.
- KV caches (in-memory/ephemeral): not persisted by default for Hosted; Dedicated/Private can enable periodic snapshotting (configurable).
- Prompt history & session transcripts: default 30 days; customers can opt into longer archives under contract.

2) Snapshot & exportability
- We support point-in-time exports for the control plane audit stream and for tenant data. Typical full snapshot generation (control-plane audit + request logs for a 90-day window) takes 2–8 hours depending on size; incremental exports (delta since last snapshot) are available and typically complete in 15–120 minutes.
- Export formats: NDJSON for event streams, Parquet for analytics-ready bulk, and gzipped CSV for ad-hoc consumption. Each export bundle includes a manifest (JSON) with checksums and a simple chain-of-custody log.

3) Redaction & DSARs
- On-demand redaction supported via a structured redaction API; exported bundles can be produced in redacted or original form with redaction provenance recorded in the manifest. We include redaction markers and a redaction.audit file that lists rules applied, operator, and timestamp.

4) Tamper evidence & integrity
- Every export includes SHA256 checksums for files and a signed export manifest. For Dedicated/Private customers we can optionally timestamp manifests via a third-party timestamping service (contracted) for verifiable timeproof.

5) SLAs & delivery timelines
- Standard: 5 business days to assemble and deliver full forensic bundle (standard S3 delivery).
- Expedited: 24–48 hours available as a billable expedite with priority job queueing.
- Delivery methods: customer-prescribed S3 with customer-managed SSE-KMS keys, encrypted SFTP, or encrypted courier for offline media.

6) Roles & access
- Exports can be triggered by users with the "Export Admin" role in the Console or via API keys with the export:trigger scope. All export actions are recorded in the control-plane audit log with operator identity, IP, job id, and parameters.

7) Cost & operational constraints
- Primary drivers: total GB of raw events assembled, compute time for reconstructing session transcripts (esp. conversation stitching), and optional redaction processing. Exports run in a resource-isolated worker pool; during large forensic jobs we can allocate burst capacity to avoid serving impact.

Next steps: I attached the Retention_Spec_Matrix.xlsx and marked the rows that apply to Hosted vs Dedicated/Private. If acceptable, we'll follow up with an Export Runbook (sample) and a proposed timeline for a proof snapshot.

Can you confirm whether Triad prefers S3 (with customer KMS) or an encrypted SFTP endpoint for delivery? Also confirm whether you require timestamping of manifests.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 415-555-0133

Subject: Re: RFP: Data stewardship, snapshot access & preservation schedule

Thanks, Evelyn — this is helpful. A few follow-ups:

- For the timestamps/signatures: Triad requires cryptographic proof of export time for audit evidence. The third-party timestamp option sounds suitable; can you name the provider and whether the timestamp is part of the exported manifest?

- For redaction provenance: will the redaction.audit file include both rule ids and the original offsets (so we can reconcile against original transcripts)? We need enough info to validate that the redaction was applied deterministically.

- For operator audit: we also need at-rest logs of who downloaded the exported bundle and the IP/credential used. Is that captured post-delivery (for S3 we can rely on S3 access logs, but if Redwood performs transfer to customer SFTP we need a recording of Redwood operator actions).

- Cost: do you have an example estimate for a 90-day, 10TB tenant snapshot (ballpark)?

If you can respond to those four points I can take this to Triad legal and then we'll lock down delivery method.

-Martin

Martin / Sarah —

Thanks for the questions. Below are firmed-up responses and an internal commitment matrix you can rely on in procurement. If Triad wants these written into contract addenda we can provide SOW language and pricing.

1) Timestamping provider and manifest placement
- Provider: TimeSeal Labs (contracted partner).
- Placement: the export manifest (manifest.json) will contain the file checksums and an export_id. TimeSeal issues a timestamp token that we attach as timestamp.token and include a signed statement timestamp.proof.txt. Both files are included in the exported bundle.

2) Redaction provenance
- redaction.audit will include: rule_id, rule_description, operator_id (if manual), deterministic matcher hashes (redact_rule_hash), and original byte offsets where available. For privacy reasons we do not include the original plaintext in the redaction.audit but include a secure mapping to the original via checksums so Triad can independently verify deterministic application.

3) Post-delivery operator audit
- For S3 delivery with customer KMS: access logs are collected via S3 server access logging; Redwood will also record the export delivery event in our control-plane audit (export_id, operator_id, delivery_uri, time). For SFTP transfers, the transfer worker records start/finish, operator job id, and destination host; we will provide those logs in the same export bundle if Triad requests them.

4) Ballpark cost for 90-day / 10TB snapshot
- Baseline assembly compute & storage egress: estimated $6,200–$9,500 (one-time) depending on redaction complexity. Expedited delivery (24–48h) adds a premium ~35%–50% depending on job queue depth.

Additional commitments and notes:
- SLA: Standard (5 business days) and Expedited (24–48 hours) as previously stated. We maintain job-level monitoring and will provide a delivery tracking id.
- Incremental exports: supported and recommended to reduce cost (typical incremental is ~10–15% of full).
- Legal: Laura, we recommend a short contract addendum: include timestamping as a charged option and require customer-provisioned KMS for the strongest chain-of-custody assurances.

If that works we can draft the SOW and an example addendum. Evelyn — I'll prepare a short export-job checklist and a sample manifest schema.

— Rishi Malhotra
